question.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\{1,4,9,16\}$. Then the number of many-one functions $f: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ such that $1 \in f(\mathrm{~A})$ is equal to :

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned}
& A=\{1,2,3,4\} \\
& B=\{1,4,9,16\}
\end{aligned}$

Total number of functions $=4^4$
Total number of one-one functions $=4!$
Total number of many one functions $=4^4-4!=232$
Total number of many-one functions in which $1 \notin f(A)=3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3=81$
$\therefore$ Total number of many one functions $1 \notin f(A)$
$\begin{aligned}
& =232-81 \\
& =151
\end{aligned}$
